s.description: Evaluate and enforce code quality including AI slop detection, redundant/uncentralized patterns, unnecessary abstraction, dead code, naming discipline, and overall code hygiene

scope.directories: src/, lib/, components/, hooks/, utils/, helpers/, services/, shared/

code_quality_system.requirement: MANDATORY: Code must be concise, centralized where shared, free of AI-generated slop, and written with intent rather than volume

spec_document.auto_create: If not exists, create code quality standards spec
spec_document.format:
## Quality Philosophy - Every line must earn its place. If it doesn't serve the user or the developer, delete it. - Shared logic lives in ONE place. Duplication is a bug. - Abstractions must pay for themselves. Premature abstraction is worse than duplication. - AI-generated code is guilty until proven innocent.
## Slop Registry - Known AI slop patterns (documented, auto-detected) - Slop score threshold for merge blocking
## Centralization Map | Shared Concern | Canonical Location | Consumers | Last Audited | - Utility functions - Shared components - Type definitions - Constants / config - API client patterns - Error handling patterns
## Naming Conventions - File naming - Component naming - Hook naming - Type/interface naming - Constant naming
## Dead Code Policy - Detection method - Cleanup schedule - Owner assignment for cleanup
## Connected Systems - Cross-reference: design-specs.md (component library = centralized UI) - Cross-reference: state-specs.md (shared state patterns) - Cross-reference: testing-specs.md (test quality mirrors code quality)

architecture_principles.principle: No line of code should exist without justification. Volume is not value.
If two files contain the same logic, one of them is wrong. Shared concerns have ONE home.
An abstraction that is used once, or that makes code harder to read, is worse than the duplication it "solves".
A good name eliminates the need for a comment. A bad name creates the need for three.
Code that reads like a chatbot wrote it (verbose, over-commented, redundantly structured) ships confusion to the next developer.
When in doubt, remove code. Dead code, dead imports, dead comments are active liabilities.

anti_patterns.violation: Verbose wrapper functions that add no logic (e.g., fetchUser that just calls fetch('/api/user'))
Comments that restate the code ("// increment counter" above counter++)
Redundant type annotations where inference is sufficient
Over-abstracted folder structures for simple apps (factory-provider-adapter for a CRUD form)
Unnecessary try/catch that just rethrows or logs and rethrows
Functions that exist to satisfy a "clean code" rule but add indirection with no value
Exhaustive JSDoc on self-documenting functions
Overly defensive null checks where types guarantee presence
Boolean variable names that need negation to read naturally (isNotDisabled, hasNoErrors)
Console-friendly error messages that no human will ever read
Same utility function defined in 2+ files
Same component rebuilt in different features instead of shared
Same type/interface defined in multiple locations
Same API call pattern repeated without shared client
Same validation logic in form and API handler
Same error handling pattern copy-pasted across services
Same color/spacing values hardcoded instead of design tokens
Same string constants defined in multiple files
Dead imports
Dead exports (exported but never imported)
Commented-out code blocks
TODO/FIXME/HACK without issue reference
Functions exceeding 40 lines (excluding templates)
Files exceeding 300 lines
More than 3 levels of nesting
Inconsistent file naming convention
Unused function parameters
Magic numbers without named constants

ai_slop_detection.description: AI-generated code has recognizable patterns. This section defines the slop signatures and how to detect them.

signature.name: parrot-comments
signature.description: Comments that restate what the code already says
signature.detection: Comment on line N restates the semantic meaning of line N+1

signature.name: wrapper-functions-to-nowhere
signature.description: Functions that wrap another call with zero additional logic, error handling, or transformation
signature.detection: Function body is only: call another function, maybe parse result, return it. No error handling, no transformation, no conditional logic.

signature.name: over-typed-obvious
signature.description: Explicit type annotations where TypeScript inference handles it
signature.example_good: const name = 'Alice' const count = 0 const isActive = true const users = await fetchUsers() // Return type inferred from fetchUsers const handleClick = (e: React.MouseEvent) => { ... }
signature.detection: Type annotation matches what the initializer/return already provides

signature.name: unnecessary-abstraction-layers
signature.description: Factory-provider-adapter-strategy patterns for simple CRUD operations
signature.example_good: // UserForm.tsx - one file, contains form + validation + types // If it grows beyond 200 lines, THEN extract
signature.detection: File count for a feature exceeds reasonable complexity. Support files outnumber feature files 3:1+.

signature.name: defensive-redundancy
signature.description: Null/undefined checks where the type system already guarantees presence
signature.detection: Null check on non-nullable type. Optional chaining on required property.

signature.name: try-catch-rethrow
signature.description: Try/catch blocks that catch, log, and rethrow without adding context or handling
signature.detection: catch block only contains: log + rethrow, or just rethrow

signature.name: chatbot-variable-naming
signature.description: Overly verbose or overly generic names that smell like generated code
signature.detection: Variable name contains 4+ concatenated nouns/adjectives. Name restates the full call chain.

signature.name: exhaustive-jsdoc-on-obvious
signature.description: JSDoc blocks that describe what is already clear from the function signature
signature.detection: JSDoc @param description matches parameter name. @returns describes the return type. Function name already communicates purpose.

slop_scoring.description: Calculate a slop density score per file

thresholds.threshold: 30%+: Unreviewed AI dump, should not merge

centralization_audit.description: Detect code that should be shared but has been duplicated across features

category.name: component-clones
category.description: Same UI component rebuilt in different features
category.detection: - Scan for components with similar prop interfaces - Scan for similar JSX structure across features - Check if a shared/ or common/ directory exists but is bypassed

category.name: utility-clones
category.description: Same helper function defined in multiple places
category.detection: - Scan for functions with identical or near-identical bodies - Check for formatDate, formatCurrency, debounce, etc. defined more than once

category.name: type-clones
category.description: Same interface/type defined in multiple files
category.detection: - Scan for identical interface shapes across files - Check if shared types live in a canonical location

category.name: pattern-clones
category.description: Same structural pattern (API call, error handling, form validation) reimplemented per feature
category.detection: - Scan for repeated fetch-then-parse patterns - Scan for repeated form validation structures - Scan for repeated error boundary patterns

centralization_rules.rule: If a piece of logic appears in 2+ features, it MUST be extracted to shared/
shared/ has a flat structure: shared/components/, shared/hooks/, shared/utils/, shared/types/
Shared code must be more general than any single consumer (no feature-specific logic in shared/)
Premature extraction is also a violation: do NOT extract to shared/ until 2+ consumers exist

criterion.name: AI Slop Density
criterion.grade: 30%+ slop density; clearly unreviewed AI output; parrot comments, wrapper-to-nowhere, over-typed throughout
15-30% slop density; some AI artifacts cleaned up but significant residue remains
5-15% slop density; mostly human-quality but AI patterns detectable in spots
Under 5% slop density; code reads as intentionally written; rare minor slop
Near-zero slop; every comment adds value; every abstraction justified; code is lean
Code that reads like literature; not a single wasted line; naming so precise comments are unnecessary; junior devs learn from reading it

criterion.name: Centralization Discipline
criterion.grade: Rampant duplication; same components/utils/types rebuilt per feature; no shared/ directory
shared/ exists but bypassed; 3+ instances of same logic across codebase
Most shared concerns centralized; some duplication in newer features
Consistent centralization; shared/ is canonical; new features use shared patterns
Zero unjustified duplication; centralization map documented; shared patterns discoverable
Shared code is a curated internal library with clear API, versioning, deprecation; acts as a force multiplier across all features; new features compose from shared primitives, never reinvent

criterion.name: Abstraction Justification
criterion.grade: Abstractions everywhere with no justification; factory-adapter-provider for a counter; 10 files for 30 lines of UI
Over-abstracted in some areas; under-abstracted in others; no consistent judgment
Most abstractions justified; occasional premature extraction or unnecessary indirection
Abstractions pay their rent; complexity proportional to the problem; easy to trace call paths
Every abstraction has 2+ consumers or clear future justification; zero indirection-for-indirection's-sake
Abstraction boundaries feel inevitable; code naturally factored at the right seams; adding a new feature requires touching exactly the right number of files (no more, no fewer)

criterion.name: Naming Precision
criterion.grade: Names are misleading, overly generic (data, info, handler, manager), or chatbot-verbose (userDataResponseFromApi)
Mix of good and bad names; some misleading; some too generic
Names are functional but not evocative; require context to understand
Names communicate intent clearly; consistent conventions; rare ambiguity
Names are precise enough that comments are unnecessary; conventions documented and enforced
Naming is a design tool; names create a ubiquitous language that maps to domain concepts; reading the code teaches you the domain

criterion.name: Dead Code & Cruft
criterion.grade: Commented-out code blocks, dead imports, unused exports, TODO graveyards throughout
Some dead code; commented blocks in non-obvious places; orphan files
Mostly clean; occasional dead import or stale TODO
No dead code; no commented blocks; TODOs have issue references; imports clean
Zero cruft; automated dead code detection in CI; unused exports caught pre-merge
Codebase is pruned as a discipline; every file, export, and function is reachable and necessary; tree-shaking reports are part of build health

criterion.name: Function & File Brevity
criterion.grade: Functions exceeding 100 lines; files exceeding 500 lines; 4+ nesting levels common
Some long functions; most files manageable; nesting occasionally deep
Most functions under 40 lines; most files under 300 lines; rare deep nesting
Consistent brevity; functions focused; files cohesive; nesting under 3 levels
Functions are tight; files have single responsibility; complexity pushed to composition rather than nesting
Every function fits in a viewport; files tell a single story; complexity is distributed across well-named, composable units that each do one thing perfectly

criterion.name: Error Handling Quality
criterion.grade: Silent swallows, catch-log-rethrow everywhere, generic "Something went wrong" for all errors
Some error handling but inconsistent; mix of swallowed and rethrown; error types vague
Errors handled but not typed; catch blocks add some context; user-facing messages generic
Typed error hierarchy; errors transformed at boundaries; user-facing messages meaningful
Error handling is a designed system: typed errors, boundary transforms, recovery paths, user-facing messages, logging with context
Errors are first-class domain concepts; error handling is invisible to business logic (handled at boundaries); error recovery is automated where possible; error reporting drives product decisions

criterion.name: Conditional Brevity
criterion.grade: Deeply nested if/else chains; ternary hell; same condition checked in multiple places
Some early returns but inconsistent; ternaries nested 2+ levels
Early returns used; conditional logic mostly flat; occasional deep branch
Guard clauses standard; ternaries single-level; switch/match used appropriately
Conditional logic is minimal and flat; polymorphism or strategy pattern replaces complex branches; easy to trace all paths
Conditionals are so well-structured they read as decision tables; every branch is testable in isolation; cyclomatic complexity is a tracked metric

slop_analysis.finding: 14 parrot comments in 40 lines of code
Every type annotation is redundant (inference handles all)
checkIfUserIsAdmin is a one-liner wrapped in ceremony

example.description: Centralization failure: same component in 3 features

example.code:
features/settings/ ToggleSettingFactory.ts // Creates toggle instances ToggleSettingProvider.tsx // React context for toggles ToggleSettingContext.ts // Context type definitions ToggleSettingReducer.ts // State management for a boolean ToggleSettingActions.ts // Action creators for a boolean ToggleSettingSelectors.ts // Selectors for a boolean ToggleSettingTypes.ts // 3 type definitions ToggleSetting.tsx // The actual 15-line component
// 8 files, ~200 lines, to manage a boolean

step.details: - Run each slop signature detector across codebase - Calculate slop density per file - Flag files above 15% threshold - Identify worst offenders

- Scan for component/utility/type clones across features - Check if shared/ directory exists and is used - Map duplicated concerns with file locations - Verify shared code is more general than consumers
- Count files per feature; flag support:feature ratio above 3:1 - Check abstractions have 2+ consumers - Identify indirection-for-indirection's-sake
- Scan for chatbot-verbose names - Scan for generic names (data, info, handler, manager, utils) - Check naming convention consistency
- Scan for dead imports - Scan for unused exports - Scan for commented-out code blocks - Scan for TODOs without issue refs
- Flag functions over 40 lines - Flag files over 300 lines - Flag nesting over 3 levels - Flag nested ternaries
Assign F-S with specific evidence and file references
- Slop report with per-file density scores - Centralization map with clone locations - Refactored code samples - Update code-quality-specs.md

output_requirements.requirement: Grade all rubric criteria with evidence and file references
Generate centralization map (duplicated concern -> file locations)
List violations by severity and category (ai-slop, centralization, hygiene)
Provide before/after refactors for worst offenders

instructions.instruction: Run slop signature detection BEFORE grading. Quantify, don't just identify.
Centralization audit must compare file contents, not just names
A file with 30%+ slop density should NEVER merge without cleanup
Same component in 2+ features without shared extraction is ALWAYS critical
Abstractions with a single consumer are suspects. Abstractions with zero consumers are dead code.
Reserve S grades for codebases where every line is load-bearing and reading the code teaches you the domain
Remember: The best code is code you didn't write. Delete aggressively.

standardization_check.step: Run slop signature scan: parrot comments, wrapper functions, over-typed, chatbot names, jsdoc restating signature, try-catch-rethrow
Calculate slop density per file; flag files above threshold
Scan for duplicated components, utilities, types across features
Verify shared/ directory exists and is canonical for shared concerns
Count files per feature; flag abstraction overengineering
Scan for dead imports, unused exports, commented-out blocks
Flag functions over 40 lines, files over 300 lines, nesting over 3 levels
Verify error handling is typed, contextual, and not catch-log-rethrow
Verify code-quality-specs.md exists and cross-references design-specs.md, state-specs.md
Report violations inline with severity and category
